title: Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act

claims.claim: Keeps the Congressional Award Program running by pushing back the date its governing board is set to shut down.
claims.note: Bill strikes the Board's Oct 1, 2023 termination date; 808 confirms the Board is the terminating body.

claims.claim: The program gives medals to young people aged 14 through 23.
claims.note: Source spells out 'fourteen through twenty-three'; numeral form is the same figure.

claims.claim: ...for achievement in public service, personal development, and physical fitness.
claims.sourceSpan: public service, personal development, and physical and expedition fitness
claims.note: Source reads 'physical and expedition fitness'; summary compresses to 'physical fitness', dropping the 'expedition' category. Minor incompleteness; top_lines carries the full phrase.

claims.claim: Extends the Congressional Award Board's termination date to October 1, 2028.
claims.note: Bill inserts 'October 1, 2028' for the struck 2023 date in Section 108 (808).

claims.claim: ...keeping the youth award program alive.
claims.sourceSpan: responsible for administering the Congressional Award Program described under section 802 of this title
claims.note: The Board administers the youth award program; extending its life keeps the program alive.

claims.claim: Awards medals to youths aged 14 through 23 nationwide.
claims.sourceSpan: medals shall be awarded to young people within the United States
claims.note: 'nationwide' = 'within the United States'; age range in same sentence.

claims.claim: Recognizes public service, personal development, and physical/expedition fitness.
claims.sourceSpan: public service, personal development, and physical and expedition fitness
claims.note: Verbatim match to the program's stated focus areas.

claims.claim: Run by the Congressional Award Board, not a federal agency.
claims.sourceSpan: The Board shall not be an agency or instrumentality of the United States
claims.note: 'not a federal agency' = 'shall not be an agency or instrumentality of the United States'.

claims.claim: Board termination date moved from Oct. 1, 2023 to Oct. 1, 2028.
claims.note: Bill: striking '2023' and inserting '2028' in Section 108 (808).

claims.claim: Extension applies retroactively as if enacted Oct. 1, 2023.
claims.sourceSpan: shall take effect as if enacted on
claims.note: Retroactive Effective Date: amendment takes effect as if enacted on October 1, 2023.

claims.claim: Drops the fixed gold-plate/rhodium/bronze medal material requirement.
claims.sourceSpan: consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or
claims.note: Bill SEC 3(1) strikes the sentence prescribing this material composition. Direction = removal, matches source.

claims.claim: Names the Act the "Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act".
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the
claims.note: Short-title clause cites the Act by that name.

claims.claim: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.note: Section 1 heading is SHORT TITLE; carries only the citation name.

claims.claim: Extends the Congressional Award Board's termination date from October 1, 2023 to October 1, 2028.
claims.note: Both dates verbatim in bill; 808 confirms it is the Board's termination date.

claims.claim: Amends Section 108 of the Congressional Award Act (2 U.S.C. 808), which sets the date the Board shall terminate.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 108 of the Congressional Award Act
claims.note: Bill names Section 108 (2 U.S.C. 808); 808 text: 'The Board shall terminate October 1, 2023.'

claims.claim: The extension takes effect retroactively as if enacted on October 1, 2023, so the Board is treated as never having lapsed.
claims.sourceSpan: shall take effect as if enacted on
claims.note: 'never having lapsed' is a fair gloss on backdating to the old termination date; matches the pattern of 808's savings provisions ('no lapse or termination of the Board ever occurred').

claims.claim: The Board administers the Congressional Award Program that awards medals to young people aged 14 through 23.
claims.note: 801: Board administers the program; 802(a): medals to young people aged fourteen through twenty-three.

claims.claim: Removes the fixed material specification for Congressional Award medals.
claims.sourceSpan: consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or
claims.note: Bill strikes the material-composition sentence; direction = removal.

claims.claim: Amends Section 102 of the Congressional Award Act (2 U.S.C. 802).
claims.sourceSpan: Section 102 of the Congressional Award Act (2 U.S.C. 802) is
claims.note: Verbatim citation in bill SEC 3.

claims.claim: It strikes the sentence in subsection (a) requiring each medal to consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze and be struck per subsection (f).
claims.sourceSpan: bronze and shall be struck in accordance with subsection (f).
claims.note: Bill SEC 3(1) strikes exactly this sentence from subsection (a).

claims.claim: ...and in subsection (f)(1) strikes "Subject to subsection (a), the" and inserts "The".
claims.note: Bill SEC 3(2): striking 'Subject to subsection (a), the' and inserting 'The' in (f)(1) second sentence.

claims.claim: The Secretary of the Treasury strikes the medals in such quantity, design, and specifications as the Secretary determines after consulting the Board.
claims.sourceSpan: the medals shall be of such quantity, design, and specifications as the Secretary of the Treasury may determine, after consultation with the Board
claims.note: Describes the post-amendment (f)(1) text; correct actor (Secretary of the Treasury) and process.

claims.claim: Strikes the statutory requirement that each medal be gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze.
claims.sourceSpan: consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or
claims.note: Matches the struck sentence.

claims.claim: ...and removes the cross-reference tying the Treasury's striking authority to that material list.
claims.note: 'Subject to subsection (a)' is the cross-reference to subsection (a)'s material list; bill strikes it.

claims.claim: Section 3 makes a separate substantive change to what the medals must be made of rather than to the program's authorization.
claims.note: SEC 3 is a distinct 'Other Amendments' section addressing medal composition, separate from the SEC 2 termination-date extension.

claims.claim: The bill extends the Board's termination date to October 1, 2028 but does not itself appropriate funds or change how the program is funded.
claims.note: Absence claim: bill has only SEC 1-3 (short title, termination date, medal material); no appropriation language. Existing 802(f)(3) funding authority is untouched.

claims.claim: Section 3 removes the required medal materials but does not specify any replacement material standard, leaving composition to the Secretary of the Treasury's determination.
claims.sourceSpan: the medals shall be of such quantity, design, and specifications as the Secretary of the Treasury may determine, after consultation with the Board
claims.note: Post-amendment (f)(1) leaves specifications to the Secretary; bill sets no replacement material.

claims.claim: The bill reauthorizes the Board through October 1, 2028 but sets no new standards, conditions, or oversight requirements on the program it revives.
claims.note: Absence claim: the two amendments are date extension + medal material; no new standards/oversight added.

claims.note: Verbatim in bill header.

claims.note: Approval date verbatim.

claims.claim: ...reauthorizing an existing youth-recognition program by extending its board's termination date...
claims.note: Bill extends the Board's termination date; 802 establishes the youth program.

claims.note: Editorial scope characterization. Structurally plausible (3 short sections, 2 amendments) but a subjective gloss with no source line. Benign.

claims.claim: ...that drew no recorded opposition...

The bill DID draw recorded opposition. (Senate passage was by voice/UC with no roll call, but the blanket 'no recorded opposition' is false given the 22 House nays.)

claims.claim: ...clearing both chambers before being signed.
claims.note: Legislative history records Senate (Oct 20) and House (Dec 15) passage, then Approved Dec 26, 2025.

claims.claim: Congressional Award Board termination date extended from October 1, 2023 to October 1, 2028, retroactive to October 1, 2023 (2 U.S.C. 808).
claims.note: Dates, retroactivity, and 808 cite all verbatim in bill SEC 2.

claims.claim: Medal material requirement changed: strikes the gold-plate-over-bronze / rhodium-over-bronze / bronze specification and the "Subject to subsection (a)" limit on the Treasury's striking authority (2 U.S.C. 802).
claims.note: Both strikes (material spec + 'Subject to subsection (a)') verbatim in bill SEC 3.

claims.claim: The statutory requirement that each Congressional Award medal consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze (2 U.S.C. 802(a)).
